summary.text: A small Solar System body is an object in the Solar System that is neither a planet, a dwarf planet, nor a natural satellite.
The group covers all comets and all minor planets other than the dwarf planets.
The orbits of the vast majority of them lie in two areas, the asteroid belt and the Kuiper belt.

facts.label: First defined
facts.value: In 2006 by the International Astronomical Union

facts.label: Members
facts.value: Comets, trojans, centaurs, and most asteroids

facts.label: Left out
facts.value: Interstellar objects passing through, such as 2I/Borisov

facts.label: Other homes
facts.value: Near-Earth asteroids, centaurs, comets and scattered disc objects

facts.label: Moons versus them
facts.value: Apart from the largest, moons differ by orbit, not size

items.prompt: Astronomers count most asteroids as small Solar System bodies. Where does Ceres, a dwarf planet, stand?

options.label: Included, because it is also an asteroid
Excluded, because dwarf planets are left out
Included, because it is bigger than most others
Excluded, because it orbits a planet, not the Sun

items.explain: The group takes in classical asteroids except the dwarf planet Ceres, since dwarf planets are not small Solar System bodies.

items.prompt: Two rocks of about equal size exist, one circling the Sun and one circling a planet. What marks the difference between them?

options.label: What they orbit: the Sun or another object
Their size, since moons are always larger
What each one is made of, rock versus ice
How bright each looks from Earth at night

items.explain: Moons differ from small Solar System bodies not in size but in their orbits, which are centered on planets or other objects, not the Sun.

items.prompt: An object that formed around another star drifts through our Solar System. Does the definition count it?

options.label: Yes, because it is passing so close to the Sun
Yes, but only if it crosses the asteroid belt
Yes, once it is bright enough to be seen easily
No, interstellar objects passing through are excluded

items.explain: The definition excludes interstellar objects traveling through the Solar System.

items.prompt: A survey maps where the vast majority of small Solar System bodies orbit. Where will it find them?

options.label: Spread evenly across the whole Solar System
Close to the Sun, inside the orbit of Mercury
In two areas: the asteroid belt and the Kuiper belt
Mostly in rings circling each of the giant planets

items.explain: The orbits of the vast majority lie in the asteroid belt and the Kuiper belt.

items.prompt: The asteroid belt and Kuiper belt show internal structure and loosely defined edges. What shapes them?

options.label: Disturbances from major planets, mainly Jupiter and Neptune
Collisions with objects arriving from other stars
Pressure from the solar wind pushing steadily on dust
Heat from the Sun melting the ice and rock inside

items.explain: Both belts have structure related to perturbations by the major planets, particularly Jupiter for the asteroid belt and Neptune for the Kuiper belt.

items.prompt: Some larger small Solar System bodies may someday be reclassified as dwarf planets. What would need to be examined?

options.label: Whether a probe has ever flown past them
Whether they are in hydrostatic equilibrium
Whether they glow with a visible gas tail
Whether they orbit inside or outside Neptune

items.explain: Reclassification depends on further examination of whether they are in hydrostatic equilibrium.
